name: Tax Identification Number (TIN)
issuer: the Director of Customs and Inland Revenue
note: The Tax Administration Act No. 37 of 2018, Part 2 Division 1, as the Department of Customs and Inland Revenue publishes it, read 2026-10-31: a person subject to a tax law must apply to the Director for a TIN, in the approved form with evidence of identity (s. 3); the Director, once satisfied of the applicant's identity, issues a unique TIN by written notice (s. 4(1), (3)); a person has one TIN at a time (s. 4(7)). The Department's page 'Tax Identification Numbers' (read 2026-10-31): TINs apply from 1 January 2020 under Part 2 of the Act; a person or entity must apply for one for all tax and licensing purposes if VAT-registered, filing rent tax returns, holding a business licence, licensing a vehicle or applying for a driver's licence; an earlier CT number becomes the TIN. The length is the Department's own: its Vanuatu Sales Monitoring System registration form (the PDF dated 1 September 2025, read 2026-10-31) asks 'Enter your TIN Number (6 Digit)'; its article 'Inland Revenue Clarifies Customs Tax Numbers' (in its archived articles, undated; read 2026-10-31) says CT numbers, of five digits at first, had six after the Revenue Management System's upgrade in 2009. READINGS: the six digits are read as every TIN's length, the VSMS form (for businesses) stating it of the TIN in general and the CT numbers, which became TINs, having six since 2009; no structure or check digit is given, so the pattern holds any six digits; 'who' is read as anyone, the Act requiring a TIN of every person subject to a tax law, citizen or not; 'needed' as tax (the page's licensing purposes aren't among the form's terms). The Act's amendments since 2018 weren't looked for. No fee, time or age is stated.

sources.title: Tax Administration Act No. 37 of 2018, as the Department of Customs and Inland Revenue publishes it
sources.said: must apply to the Director for a taxpayer identification number unless the person has already been issued with a TIN ... the Director must issue a TIN by serving the applicant with written notice of the TIN. ... Each TIN issued by the Director must be unique. ... A person can have only one TIN at any time.
